name: The Hyundai Seoul
summary: Seoul's largest department store: sunlit glass-roofed atriums, an indoor garden, a 12 m waterfall and nonstop pop-ups in Yeouido.
description: Opened in 2021 in the Parc.1 complex, The Hyundai Seoul gives almost half its floor area to open space, gardens and a glass roof that floods the atriums with daylight. Luxury and contemporary labels share the floors with a rotating programme of brand pop-ups and art exhibitions that draw young Seoul on weekends. The basement food hall is one of the city's biggest, and the 5th-floor Sounds Forest indoor garden is the place to sit down. It is the most 'future Seoul' of the city's department stores and an easy half-day with parents.
highlights: Sounds Forest indoor garden under the glass roof (5F)
12-metre indoor waterfall and daylight-filled atrium
Rotating brand pop-ups and exhibitions (B1–B2 and event halls)
Huge basement food hall and dessert counters
tips: CLOSED Thu 24 and Fri 25 Sep for Chuseok (Hyundai Department Store notice); go Sat 26 onwards.
From home, Line 3 to Express Bus Terminal then Line 9 express to Yeouido is the fastest subway route; the store connects underground from Yeouido Station.
Weekend afternoons are packed with pop-up queues — arrive at 10:30 opening or on a weekday.
Foreign shoppers can claim tax refunds; bring passports for all five.

tripadvisor.rank: #149 of 1,622 things to do in Seoul

reviews.text: This is the most pleasant and beautiful mall I have ever seen. We enjoy going there, the shops are well distributed on all floors.
The Hyundai Seoul is absolutely stunning—a modern, sleek shopping centre that feels like a luxury experience from the moment you walk in.
Visit Seoul notes it has become a Yeouido landmark thanks to constant pop-up stores, exhibitions and seasonal indoor landscaping that create photo zones.

price.note: Free to browse; mix of luxury and contemporary brands, food hall for casual meals

hours.note: Restaurants to 22:00. Hyundai stores also close one designated day per month (usually a Monday); in September 2026 the closure is 24–25 Sep.

chuseok.note: Closed Thu 24 and Fri 25 Sep (Hyundai's 11 stores incl. The Hyundai Seoul); open from Sat 26.

name: Shinsegae Department Store Gangnam
summary: Korea's top-grossing department store, right above Express Bus Terminal: Sweet Park dessert hall, House of Shinsegae dining, luxury floors.
description: Shinsegae Gangnam sits on top of Express Bus Terminal station, one stop from home on Line 3, and is the store Seoulites treat as the benchmark. Its renovated food floors are the draw: Sweet Park (opened Feb 2024) packs 43 dessert brands into about 5,300 m² of Grand Central-style arcades, House of Shinsegae (June 2024) is a dim, hotel-like dining and wine hall open until 22:00, and Shinsegae Market sells premium produce and gifts. Above them are every major luxury house, Korean designers and a big beauty floor. Easy to pop into repeatedly during the week.
highlights: Sweet Park — Korea's largest dessert hall (43 brands incl. Pierre Marcolini, Mille & Un, Fortnum & Mason)
House of Shinsegae — low-lit restaurant hall and ~5,000-bottle Wine Cellar, open to 22:00
Shinsegae Market premium grocery and Chuseok gift sets
Full luxury and K-beauty floors under one roof
tips: NEAR HOME: one stop on Line 3 to Express Bus Terminal (or a short taxi); combine with Goto Mall underneath.
CLOSED Thu 24 and Fri 25 Sep; open Sat 26 onward (extended hours to 20:30 Fri–Sun).
House of Shinsegae restaurants stay open to 22:00 (last order 1 h before) — good for a late family dinner after the store closes.
Spend ₩50,000+ for 1 h free parking; foreign shoppers get tax refunds on eligible purchases (bring passports).

tripadvisor.rank: #63 of 1,622 things to do in Seoul

reviews.text: Excellent and elegant shopping and food center just next to the JW Marriott Hotel and bus terminal.

reviews.text: Colossal shopping mall with wide range of merchandise and food choices + easy access to subway and trains.
reviews.author: Yosemite008

reviews.text: Seoul Economic Daily: House of Shinsegae 'opened the department store's night' — lighting at a quarter of normal store levels, hotel-style private rooms and a wine cellar staff say stocks what nowhere else in Korea does.
The renovated Gangnam food hall passed 10 million cumulative shoppers in its first year, helped by chef-collaboration brands.

price.note: Free to browse; desserts and food-hall meals are the affordable way in, luxury floors upward

hours.note: Official calendar: extended hours (to 20:30) Fri–Sun and Sat 26/Sun 27 Sep. Restaurant floor 11:00–21:30; House of Shinsegae 10:30–22:00.

chuseok.note: Closed Thu 24 and Fri 25 Sep (Shinsegae Gangnam and 10 other stores); open with extended hours Sat 26 and Sun 27.

name: Shinsegae Department Store Main Store & The Heritage
summary: Korea's first department store (1930s building) plus The Heritage, a restored 1935 bank with Korean craft floor and a giant media facade.
description: Shinsegae's flagship faces the Bank of Korea roundabout between Myeongdong and Namdaemun Market: an early-20th-century main building joined to a modern wing. Across the lane, The Heritage (opened 9 April 2025) restores a 1935 bank — Seoul cultural heritage — with a Peter Marino-designed Chanel on 1–2F, a 4F museum of Myeongdong's retail history and House of Shinsegae Heritage on 5F showcasing Korean crafts with a dessert salon. After dark the store's wraparound digital media facade lights the whole square. The basement food hall is a long-time office-lunch favourite.
highlights: The Heritage: restored 1935 bank, 5F House of Shinsegae Heritage Korean craft gallery-shop and dessert salon
Shinsegae Square media facade on the main building after dark
4F museum on Myeongdong's retail history with restored 1930s–50s images
Basement food hall (11:00–21:30)
tips: CLOSED Fri 25 and Sat 26 Sep (Main store closes 25–26, unlike Gangnam); open Thu 24 and from Sun 27.
Line 4 Hoehyeon Station Exit 7 leads straight in; pair with Namdaemun Market (next door) or Myeongdong (5 min walk) — but Namdaemun is shut 24–27 Sep.
Come just after sunset to see the media facade, then eat in the food hall.
The Heritage follows the store's closing days (Chuseok and monthly closure).

reviews.text: Shinsegae is Seoul's answer to Harrods or Macy's. Its Myeongdong store is a de facto landmark in downtown.

reviews.author: Ame S

price.note: Free to browse; museum/craft floors free, luxury retail and dessert salon at premium prices

hours.note: Food hall 11:00–21:30. Official calendar shows extended hours Thu 24 and Sun 27 Sep.

chuseok.note: Main store (and The Heritage) closed Fri 25 and Sat 26 Sep; open Thu 24 with extended hours and from Sun 27.

name: Spa Lei (women only)
summary: Women-only 24h bathhouse by Sinsa Station: seawater and open-air baths, a pine-fired bulhanjeungmak and famous body scrubs.
description: Spa Lei is a women-only sauna and jjimjilbang in Jamwon-dong, a few minutes' walk from Sinsa Station and one stop from home on Line 3. The spa styles itself on Eastern European bathhouses, with dark wood, framed photographs and a small open-air bath on a terrace, alongside a West Coast seawater bath, green-tea bath and a cold plunge that regulars rave about. The traditional bulhanjeungmak (fire-heated dome sauna) is lit with Gangwon pine at 5 am and opens at 10 am; there are also red-clay, charcoal and salt rooms. Seshin (Korean body scrub), oil massage, facials and nails are sold in-house, which is what most foreign reviewers come for.
highlights: Seshin body scrub, with oil or aroma add-ons
Pine-fired bulhanjeungmak dome sauna (opens 10:00)
Small open-air bath and terrace
Seawater bath and ice-cold plunge
tips: Women only: the men in the family need somewhere else, such as the JW Marriott Seoul sauna nearby at Express Bus Terminal.
Entry is ₩22,000 for 8 hours, then ₩2,000 an hour. Several September 2026 Naver reviewers were surprised by the overtime charge, so note your entry time.
Spa Lei went viral on Instagram in September 2026 and Naver reviewers report packed weekends and Chuseok-season crowds. Go on a weekday morning, or just after 10:00 when the fire sauna opens.
Book scrubs and massages at the desk as soon as you arrive, because slots fill on busy days. Staff speak some English, according to TripAdvisor reviewers.

tripadvisor.rank: #13 of 512 Spas & Wellness in Seoul

reviews.text: A reviewer booked the full-body scrub and oil cleanse and called it an incredible experience, even if lying on the plastic table felt comical.
A reviewer suggests spending the whole day there. The scrub and massage cost extra but are worth it.
A regular praised the variety of baths and the 'delicious' ice-cold plunge, and liked the fire sauna. They wished pool-cleaning times were posted, because they arrived at dawn and could not bathe.
Some September 2026 reviews call it packed after going viral on Instagram, with queues at the snack bar and a full fire-sauna dome. They say to go off-peak.

price.note: Entry ₩22,000 for 8 hours, then ₩2,000 an hour. Scrubs, massage and facials are extra and priced at the desk. Parking is ₩3,000 for the first 6 hours, then ₩2,000 an hour (official site).

hours.note: Open 24 hours, every day. The bulhanjeungmak fire sauna opens at 10:00 daily. VisitKorea lists it as open year-round.

chuseok.note: Runs 24/7 and VisitKorea lists it as open year-round. Naver reviews show it operating in mid-September 2026. No 2026 Chuseok notice was found. Expect crowds on 24–26 Sep and call 02-545-4002 if you are going on the 25th.

name: SPAREX Dongmyo
summary: A modern 24h jjimjilbang on the 13th floor above Dongmyo Station, with a fire-kiln sauna, hinoki bath and city views, for ₩14,000.
description: SPAREX Dongmyo is a newer branch of the SPAREX chain, opened around 2024 on the 13th floor of the building beside Dongmyo Station. It replaces the big old-school bathhouses that closed after COVID, including Dragon Hill Spa and Siloam Sauna. It is bright and modern, with gender-separated baths and dry and wet saunas, then a shared hall in spa clothes with a bulhanjeungmak (fire-heated dome), hwangto clay, salt, ice and hinoki rooms. There is also a food court serving sikhye, roasted eggs and Korean set meals, a well-equipped gym and screen golf. Locals love it: 7,700+ Naver reviews single out how clean it is, its size and its fair price.
highlights: Bulhanjeungmak fire domes and a hinoki forest-bath room
13th-floor lounges with city views
Food court: sikhye, roasted eggs, jeyuk and miyeok-guk
Seshin body scrub packages
tips: Hidden gem: over 7,700 Naver visitor reviews but only a handful on TripAdvisor. Go straight out of Dongmyo Station Exit 6 and up to the 13th floor.
Entry is ₩14,000 from 05:00–20:00 or ₩16,000 from 20:00–05:00, valid for 24 hours. Parking is free for 3 hours (official Instagram, June 2026).
Bring your own shampoo and a few ₩1,000 notes or coins, because hairdryers are coin-operated. Baths close for cleaning late at night (women's roughly 23:00–01:00, men's 00:00–02:00).
Pair it with the Dongmyo flea market or Dongdaemun (one stop on Line 1 or 6). It is also a cheap, rainy-evening reset for a group of 5.

reviews.text: A September 2026 reviewer found everything clean because it is fairly new. They liked the high-floor views, the jeyuk and seaweed-soup dinner and the reasonable price, and plan to return.
Another reviewer found the scrub short and the food-court tteokbokki and ramyeon undercooked. They called the food the weak spot.
A traveller said their scrub was excellent and very thorough, and that they 'felt like a new woman'.
A first-timer said nobody explained how the spa worked. Know the routine (shoe locker, bath, spa clothes) before you go.

price.note: ₩14,000 for entry 05:00–20:00 or ₩16,000 for 20:00–05:00, each valid 24 h. Scrubs and meals are extra.

hours.note: Open 24 hours, all year. Bath cleaning: women's about 23:00–01:00, men's about 00:00–02:00. No scrubs 01:00–03:00. No unaccompanied minors 22:00–05:00.

chuseok.note: Open 24/7 all year, and Naver reviews show it operating through mid-September 2026. No specific 2026 Chuseok notice was found. Holiday afternoons will be busy.

name: Supsok Hanbang Land
summary: A charcoal-kiln bathhouse on a wooded hill above Sinchon, where you roast sweet potatoes on the embers and rest on forest decks.
description: Supsok Hanbang Land (the 'forest herbal land') is one of the few Seoul jjimjilbangs that still fires real charcoal kilns (sutgama). There are low, medium and high-heat chambers, plus a hearth room where glowing charcoal sits in a brazier. It sits against Ansan's woods near Bongwonsa Temple, so between sweats you can cool off on shaded wooden decks outside. The snack bar sells sikhye and roasted eggs, and you can grill sweet potatoes, potatoes and rice cakes yourself; a separate restaurant grills samgyeopsal. Korean TV has featured it many times, and it is the most characterful of the classic big bathhouses left after Dragon Hill Spa and Siloam closed.
highlights: Charcoal kilns in three heat levels
Grill your own sweet potatoes and garaetteok (rice cakes)
Forest rest decks outdoors
Pork-belly grill restaurant on site
tips: Bring socks, or buy them for ₩3,000: you need socks and a towel underfoot in the hottest kiln.
Adult bath plus sauna was ₩17,000 in July 2026, per a Naver review. Hairdryers are coin-operated and the coin noraebang takes cash only.
It is uphill from Sinchon and Ewha, so take a taxi from Ewha Womans Univ. Station on Line 2, direct from Seocho, rather than walking the slope with parents.
Weekends get crowded and noisy with kids. Arrive early on a weekday; the kilns run 08:00–21:00.

tripadvisor.rank: #107 of 512 Spas & Wellness in Seoul

reviews.text: A visitor called it another fantastic jjimjilbang, and even better after hiking nearby Ansan.
A reviewer loved roasting sweet potatoes and rice cakes, the variety of sauna rooms and the resident cat, and called it a one-of-a-kind jjimjilbang in Seoul.
Other recent reviews say the building and ice room are dated and service can be curt. Come for the kilns, not polish.

price.note: About ₩17,000 for bath plus charcoal kiln, or about ₩11,000 for bath only (Trip.com guide and a July 2026 Naver review). Snacks and grilling are extra.

hours.note: Charcoal kiln 08:00–21:00. Not a 24h venue (Visit Seoul).

chuseok.note: Visit Seoul lists daily operation with no closure days, but no 2026 Chuseok notice was found. It will probably be open on 24 and 26 Sep. Call +82-2-365-2700 before going on Chuseok day (25 Sep).

name: Banyan Tree Spa Seoul
nameKo: 반얀트리 스파 (반얀트리 클럽 앤 스파 서울)
summary: Banyan Tree's own spa, set in the Namsan woods: private suites with baths, Asian massage and an 80-minute head spa.
description: Banyan Tree Club & Spa Seoul is an urban resort on the forested east slope of Namsan, and its spa on the lobby floor (3F, The Club) is the brand's original Asian spa concept. There are 11 treatment rooms, each with its own bathroom and rest area: 4 deluxe singles, 4 doubles, 2 spa suites and a dedicated head-spa room with ergonomic shampoo chairs. Therapists trained at Banyan Tree's academy work by hand with herbal, natural products. Every full treatment includes 30 minutes of 'Calm Time' with a foot bath and tea. It is the splurge pick for parents who want a quiet, luxurious afternoon, and it pairs easily with a Namsan walk or dinner in Jangchung-dong.
highlights: Korean Essence package: green-tea scrub, Korean traditional therapy and express facial (₩500,000)
Banyan Tree Head Spa with Leonor Greyl, 80 min
Couples and double rooms, so two parents can be treated together
Namsan forest views and the hotel's indoor pool nearby
tips: Book by phone (02-2250-8115/8116) or email Spa-Seoul@banyantree.com. Late changes or cancellations are charged at 100%.
Prices include 10% tax. A 60-minute body therapy is ₩290,000 and 90 minutes is ₩380,000. The 30-minute head-and-shoulder or foot therapy (₩150,000) is the lighter option.
Book a double room so two of you are treated together. There are 4 double rooms plus 2 spa suites.
The hotel is up the Namsan hill. Take a taxi from Dongguk Univ. Station (Line 3, direct from Nambu Bus Terminal) rather than walking.

tripadvisor.rank: #32 of 567 hotels in Seoul (hotel rating, not spa-only)

reviews.text: Warm spa room is the best thing.
A guest who stayed at three Seoul hotels rated Banyan Tree the best, citing the fantastic view and the adjoining garden.
Reviewers often praise the Namsan and N Seoul Tower views, the well-kept grounds and the resort-style facilities, which feel rare in central Seoul.

price.note: 30-min partial therapy ₩150,000; 60/90-min body therapy ₩290,000/₩380,000; head spa 80 min ₩320,000; Royal Banyan 150 min ₩585,000. Tax included (official site).

hours.note: Spa open 11:00–21:00 by reservation (official site).

chuseok.note: Luxury hotel spas normally run through Chuseok, and the official site lists no closure days. No 2026 holiday notice was found, and holiday slots sell out, so book ahead.

name: Lotte World Mall & Avenuel
summary: Seoul’s tallest-tower mall: Avenuel luxury, duty free, aquarium, K-food basement and Seoul Sky above.
description: Lotte World Mall sits at the foot of the 555 m Lotte World Tower in Jamsil and bundles a mainstream mall, the Avenuel luxury department store, Lotte Duty Free, a cinema, Lotte Mart and Lotte World Aquarium under one roof. It is the easiest one-stop rainy-day complex in Seoul for a mixed-age group, with wide corridors, lifts and plenty of seating. The basement food hall is cheaper than the upper floors, and Seokchon Lake is a pleasant walk outside. Pair it with Seoul Sky or Lotte World Adventure next door.
highlights: Avenuel luxury halls and Lotte Duty Free
Seoul Sky observatory entrance (tower)
Lotte World Aquarium in B1–B2
Basement food hall and Seokchon Lake walk
tips: Chuseok: the mall itself runs noon–22:00 on 25 Sep, but Avenuel/Lotte Department Store Jamsil is closed 24–25 Sep.
Jamsil Station (Line 2/8) Exit 11 is 84 m away; from home it is a straight Line 2 ride from Seocho or Gyodae.
Show your passport at Lotte Duty Free for tax-free prices; free stroller and wheelchair rental is available.

tripadvisor.rank: #16 of 1,622 things to do in Seoul

reviews.text: Seoul's tallest skyscraper at 555m tall is well worth the trip up. The queues were minimal early afternoon.
Reviewers split on the mall itself: huge, with every chain and Korean cosmetics brand, but upper floors are pricey while the basement food is affordable.

price.note: Free entry; mainstream to luxury shopping. Parking ₩300 per 10 min on weekdays.

hours.note: Mall 10:30–22:00; Avenuel 10:30–20:00; Lotte Duty Free 09:30–20:00; Lotte Mart 10:00–23:00; Aquarium 10:00–20:00.

name: Starfield COEX Mall & Starfield Library
summary: Asia’s largest underground mall, home to the towering bookshelves of Starfield Library, COEX Aquarium and a megaplex.
description: Starfield COEX Mall runs under the COEX convention centre in Samseong, with hundreds of Korean and global brands, a 17-screen Megabox, COEX Aquarium and the Kimchi Museum. Its centrepiece is Starfield Library (별마당도서관), a free, open atrium lined with towering bookshelves that has become one of Seoul’s most photographed interiors. Outside, the giant digital “wave” billboards around COEX K-POP Square are a futuristic bonus. Hyundai Department Store COEX (무역센터점) connects directly.
highlights: Starfield Library’s towering bookshelves (free)
COEX K-POP Square giant LED screens outside
COEX Aquarium and Megabox under one roof

name: GOTO Mall (Express Bus Terminal Underground Shopping Center)
summary: Bargain underground arcade: 620 shops of clothes, cosmetics and homewares one stop from home.
description: GOTO Mall is Gangnam’s biggest underground shopping street: about 620 small shops along two long corridors under the Express Bus Terminal. Expect cheap on-trend women’s fashion, shoes, bags, accessories, cosmetics, bedding, tableware and flowers, often in the ₩5,000–10,000 range. It links directly to Shinsegae Gangnam and the Central City food court, so it is an easy add-on to a department-store afternoon. It is loud and busy rather than polished, but the value is hard to beat.
highlights: Two ~880 m corridors of fashion, shoes and accessories
Homewares, tableware and bedding at local prices
Direct link to Shinsegae Gangnam and Central City
tips: Near home: one stop on Line 3 from Nambu Bus Terminal to Express Bus Terminal, Exit 8-1/8-2.
Go on a weekday morning; weekends are shoulder-to-shoulder.
Many stalls take cash more happily than cards; prices are usually fixed.

tripadvisor.rank: #61 of 1,622 things to do in Seoul

reviews.text: The GOTO mall is an underground bargain shoppers paradise.
Endless aisles filled with merchandise for everyone, including food, housewares, accessories, shoes and clothing!
Visitors praise quality for the price but warn it gets extremely crowded at weekends.

price.note: Many items ₩5,000–10,000

hours.note: Shops 10:00–22:00; corridors open 24 h. Open year-round except Lunar New Year and Chuseok (some shops).

name: Galleria Luxury Hall (EAST & WEST)
summary: Apgujeong’s benchmark luxury department store: EAST for the big maisons, WEST for younger labels and Gourmet 494.
description: Galleria Luxury Hall is two buildings on Apgujeong-ro facing each other across Apgujeongrodeo Station. EAST gathers the top maisons (it was the first in Korea to carry Chanel, Louis Vuitton and Hermès together), while WEST works as a large select store and hides Gourmet 494, a polished basement food hall. WEST’s glass-disc façade lights up with media art after dark. Service for international shoppers includes interpretation and styling help.
highlights: EAST: flagship luxury maisons
WEST: select-store floors and LED disc façade at night

name: The Spa at Grand Hyatt Seoul
summary: Namsan-side hotel spa with 14 suites: Korean massage and facials, plus pre-treatment sauna and pool time.
description: On the garden level of the Grand Hyatt on Namsan’s southern slope, The Spa has 14 treatment suites and rooms offering Korean massage, aromatherapy, stone and gold-oil massages, signature body treatments and facials. Guests get around 45 minutes of sauna and pool access before treatment. Reviewers rate the therapists among the best in the city, and the calm, hotel-level service suits parents who want a polished, English-speaking spa.
highlights: Korean massage and signature body treatment
45-minute sauna/pool access before treatments
Tea ritual in a lounge with a koi pool
tips: Book a few days ahead; request adjacent slots for a group.
Hangangjin Station (Line 6) is about 6 minutes on foot but uphill — a taxi to the hotel door is easier.
Arrive early to use the sauna and pool before your appointment.

name: Han River Night Picnic, Games & Starlight Cruise
summary: Guided evening in Yeouido: chimaek picnic by the river, dalgona and ttakji games, then a 50-minute Han River cruise.
description: This small-group evening tour recreates the classic Seoul night out by the Han River. An English-speaking guide sets up chairs, tables and lamps in Yeouido Hangang Park for a chicken-and-beer (chimaek) picnic with soju and snacks, teaches traditional games like dalgona and ttakji, then boards a round-trip cruise from Yanghwa pier past lit bridges and the National Assembly. It removes all the logistics of doing it yourself and is a relaxed way for a mixed-age family to see the river at night.
highlights: Chimaek picnic set up for you in Yeouido Hangang Park
Dalgona and ttakji games
50-minute Han River cruise past lit bridges
tips: Meet at Yeouinaru Station (Line 5) Exit 2; from home take Line 3 to Express Bus Terminal, Line 9 to Yeouido, then Line 5 one stop.
Evenings on the river get cool in late September — bring a light jacket.
Book with free cancellation and check the weather the day before; rain may change the picnic.

reviews.text: He transformed our evening into a beautiful memory that felt just like a joyful picnic.
It was a very pleasant experience! I had a lot of fun playing games, eating good food.
Ron was awesome... it was all fun, and Ron brought all the right energy.

price.note: From about US$99 (US$84 with the current discount) per adult on Tripadvisor; food, drinks and cruise included

hours.note: Evening departure (about 4 h); check start time when booking.

chuseok.note: Tour operator runs on scheduled dates; check the booking calendar for 24–26 Sep.

name: Lotte World Aquarium
summary: Modern aquarium under Lotte World Mall: underwater tunnel, huge ocean tank and photo zones — note TripAdvisor’s welfare flag.
description: Lotte World Aquarium fills the basement of Lotte World Mall in Jamsil with 13 themed zones modelled on the world’s oceans, an escalator-tunnel entrance, a large main ocean tank and walk-through tunnel, plus seals, otters and penguins. It is bright, modern and easy to combine with the mall and tower. TripAdvisor states that it does not currently meet its animal-welfare policy (earlier reviews raised concerns about beluga whales), so families who care about this may prefer SEA LIFE COEX.
highlights: Walk-through underwater tunnel
Large main ocean viewing panel
Seals, otters and penguins
Mirror and tunnel photo zones
tips: Combine with Lotte World Mall and Seoul Sky in one Jamsil day; Jamsil Station (Line 2/8).
Weekday mornings are calmer; buy tickets online to skip the counter.
Open daily 10:00–22:00 per TripAdvisor.

name: Insadong Spa & Sauna (Insadong Hanjeungmak)
summary: Foreigner-friendly Korean sauna near Anguk: stone kiln hanjeungmak, hot and cold baths, and a vigorous seshin body scrub.
description: Insadong Spa & Sauna is a traditional bathhouse just off Insadong with a domed stone hanjeungmak (kiln sauna), several saunas at different temperatures, gender-separated hot and cold baths and a Korean-style rest area. Its reputation comes from the brisk seshin body scrub and massage packages done by experienced staff, with English spoken at reception. It is the easiest place in central Seoul to try the full Korean scrub ritual without a language barrier.
highlights: Stone-dome hanjeungmak kiln sauna
Korean body scrub (seshin) and massage packages
Hot/cold baths and a traditional rest area
tips: No reservation needed; English-speaking reception.
Cash preferred — reviewers report a 10% surcharge on cards.
Anguk Station (Line 3, direct from Nambu Bus Terminal) is 5 min away — pair with Insadong or a palace.

name: POINT OF VIEW SEOUL
summary: Seongsu’s three-floor stationery and object store — Tool, Scene, Archive — for beautifully curated pens, paper and gifts.
description: POINT OF VIEW is a design-led stationery and goods store on Yeonmujang-gil whose three floors are themed TOOL, SCENE and ARCHIVE. It gathers well-made paper, writing instruments and inspiring desk objects from Korea and abroad, displayed like a small museum. It is a calm, grown-up counterpart to Seongsu’s pop-up queues and a source of compact, giftable souvenirs.
highlights: TOOL floor: pens, paper and desk tools
SCENE and ARCHIVE floors of curated objects
Gift-ready Korean-designed stationery
tips: Closed on the last Monday of each month — that is Mon 28 Sep 2026.
Seongsu Station (Line 2) Exit 4, ~6 min; next to Olive Young N Seongsu and Rxpert SkinLounge.
Check Instagram for holiday hours before Chuseok visits.
